'''Rainer W. Bussmann''' ([[Leutkirch]], 30 May 1967) is a German-US American botanist and vegetation ecologist, specializing in [[ethnobotany]] and [[ethnobiology]], wild food plants, wild crop relatives, climate change, gastronomic botany and preservation of [[traditional knowledge]] in the [[Andes]], the [[Caucasus]] and the [[Himalayas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3524-5273|title=Rainer W. Bussmann (0000-0002-3524-5273)|website=orcid.org}}</ref> He has worked at the [[University of Bayreuth]], [[University of Hawaii]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://manoa.hawaii.edu/news/article.php?aId=1135|title=Mānoa: UH Manoa botanist Rainer Bussmann to participate in $1.78 million research and conservation grant &#124; University of Hawaii News|website=manoa.hawaii.edu}}</ref> [[University of Texas]], the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mobot.org/events/Assets/07110RainerBussman.pdf|access-date=18 April 2023|website=mobot.org|title=Garden announces new William Brown center director|date=December 10, 2007}}</ref> [[Ilia State University]] and the [[State Museum of Natural History Karlsruhe]];<ref>{{cite web | url=https://bnn.de/karlsruhe/weltweit-bekannter-forscher-kommt-ans-naturkundemuseum-karlsruhe | title=Weltweit bekannter Forscher kommt ans Naturkundemuseum Karlsruhe | date=28 October 2022 }}</ref> he has founded several international non-governmental organizations, including Nature and Culture International, Saving Knowledge,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.savingknowledge.org/|title=Saving Knowledge|website=Saving Knowledge}}</ref> and Ethnomont.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ethnobotcaucasus.org/ethnomont|title=Ethnomont|website=Department of Ethnobotany}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
From 1994 to 2002 Bussmann worked as Post Doc at the [[University of Bayreuth]] developing ecological research in the mountain forests of [[Kenya]] and [[Ethiopia]], and as scientific coordinator of the DFG (German Science Foundation) program, "Functionality in a Tropical Mountain Rainforest: Diversity, Dynamic Processes and Utility Potentials under Ecosystem Perspectives<ref>{{Cite web|title=DFG-Forschergruppen 402 und 816 Tropischer Bergregenwald Research Units Tropical Mountain Forest|url=http://tropical-mountain-rain-forests.org/|website=tropical-mountain-rain-forests.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.focus.de/wissen/natur/fruchtbares-geheimnis-biologie_id_1952877.html|title=Fruchtbares Geheimnis|first=FOCUS|last=Online|website=FOCUS Online}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Mitglieder der DFG-Forschergruppe 402 "Tropischer Bergregenwald" – Members of the Research Unit of the DFG 402 "Tropical Mountain Rainforest" – Miembros del grupo de investigadores de la DFG 402 "Bosque Tropical Iluvioso Montañoso"|url=http://bergregenwald.de/pages/05Mitglieder.html|website=bergregenwald.de}}</ref> featured in the German television documentary series "Humboldts Erben".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fernsehserien.de/humboldts-erben/folgen/1x04-im-tal-der-hundertjaehrigen-396015|title=Humboldts Erben Staffel 1, Folge 4: Im Tal der Hundertjährigen|first=imfernsehen GmbH & Co|last=KG|date=28 January 2001 |via=www.fernsehserien.de}}</ref> During that same time he led investigations of vegetation in the forests of [[East Africa]], including the establishment of the Maseno University Botanical Garden.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biota-africa.org/hist_biota.php?histcode=e12p&Page_ID=L850_04_02&backfile=hist_east_titlesub1.php|title=BIOTA AFRICA|website=www.biota-africa.org}}</ref> Bussmann was also one of the founding participants of the Global Mountain Biodiversity Assessment ([[GMBA]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gmba.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/microsites/micro_gmba/content/e426534/e426543/e426545/e449616/MountainBiodiversityMatters.pdf|access-date=18 April 2023|website=gmba.unibe.ch|title=Mountain Biodiversity Matters}}</ref>

From 2003 to 2006 he joined the [[University of Hawaii]] (Manoa) as Scientific Director of the [[Harold L. Lyon Arboretum]], and as associate professor of botany,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.catalog.hawaii.edu/08-09/personnel/isrsustaff3.htm|title=University of Hawaii at Manoa Catalog|website=www.catalog.hawaii.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archives.starbulletin.com/2003/10/03/features/index3.html|title=Honolulu Star-Bulletin Features|website=archives.starbulletin.com}}</ref> focusing his research on the ecology of cloud forests and medicinal plants in northern Peru, under the Program of International Health Research Training and Health of Minorities (MHIRT) of the National Institute of Health.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.northperuproject.org/|title=North Peru Projects|website=North Peru Projects|access-date=3 August 2021|archive-date=13 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713153504/http://www.northperuproject.org/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.northperuproject.org/projects|title=Personnel|website=North Peru Projects|access-date=3 August 2021|archive-date=3 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803084534/http://www.northperuproject.org/projects|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.northperuproject.org/new-page-1|title=MHIRT|website=North Peru Projects}}</ref> During 2006–2007 he joined the Department of Geography at the University of Texas (Austin) as a visiting professor.

In 2007 he was appointed director of the William L. Brown Center, and William L. Brown Curator of Economic Botany<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dosingpdf.com/w/wlbcenter.org2.html|title=Qn_2007_4.indd|website=dosingpdf.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/stlouis/stories/2008/02/25/tidbits2.html|title=Rainer Bussmann. Missouri Botanical Garden|access-date=18 April 2023|website=bizjournals.com|date=25 February 2008|agency=St. Louis Business Journal|author=Diana Barr}} (subscription required)</ref> at the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]]. Over the next decade, Bussmann transformed the center into an international research unit with projects on five continents, ranging from traditional [[ethnobotany]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencebyseltzer.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/ethnobotany.pdf|access-date=18 April 2023|website=sciencebyseltzer.com|title=Ethnobotany|date=January 2012}}</ref> and [[ethnopharmacology]], to regeneration ecology, the impact of [[climate change]], [[Intellectual Property Rights]], and the application of the "[[Nagoya Protocol]] on Access to Genetic Resources and Fair and Equitable Sharing in Benefits Arising from its Use".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.plants2020.net/news/1037/|title=Call for a Global Program on Conservation of Useful Plants and Traditional Knowledge|website=www.plants2020.net}}</ref>

In 2017 he left the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]] to co-found a new Department of Ethnobotany at the Institute of Botany and Bakuriani Alpine Botanical Garden (BABG) at [[Ilia State University]], Georgia (Caucasus).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ethnobotcaucasus.org/|title=Department of Ethnobotany|website=Department of Ethnobotany}}</ref>

His standard botanical author abbreviation is Bussmann, and he has described a variety of plant species new to science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ipni.org/?q=bussmann|title=International Plant Names Index|website=www.ipni.org}}</ref>

Bussmann is recognized in the archaeological and pharmacological field for the identification of a Moche hallucinogen found in many tombs and found in the ceramics and paintings of the culture in Northern Peru, the "Ulluchu".<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Naming a phantom – the quest to find the identity of Ulluchu, an unidentified ceremonial plant of the Moche culture in Northern Peru|first1=Rainer W.|last1=Bussmann|first2=Douglas|last2=Sharon|date=31 March 2009|journal=Journal of Ethnobiology and Ethnomedicine|volume=5|issue=1|pages=8|doi=10.1186/1746-4269-5-8|pmid=19335907|pmc=2670266 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stltoday.com/news/scientists-get-dirt-on-mystery-plant-once-a-part-of-sacrifices-it-may-have-medical/article_3a5dc246-7f04-5e3a-86cd-912a1b2f2f64.html|title=Scientists get dirt on mystery plant Once a part of sacrifices, it may have medical uses.|first=Kim |last=Mcguire |website=STLtoday.com|date=5 May 2009 }}</ref>

As part of their research, Bussmann's group pays special attention to the rights of indigenous communities, supporting them in their actions generated the effect of [[global change]]. In the "Chácobo Ethnobotanical Project" they showed how indigenous researchers, trained in ethnobotanical methods, can carry out a study on the same level as university scientists. All project results, and translations of previous work, were delivered to the tribe, and local researchers participated as co-authors in all publications.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Traditional knowledge hiding in plain sight – twenty-first century ethnobotany of the Chácobo in Beni, Bolivia|first1=Narel Y.|last1=Paniagua Zambrana|first2=Rainer W.|last2=Bussmann|first3=Robbie E.|last3=Hart|first4=Araceli L.|last4=Moya Huanca|first5=Gere|last5=Ortiz Soria|first6=Milton|last6=Ortiz Vaca|first7=David|last7=Ortiz Álvarez|first8=Jorge|last8=Soria Morán|first9=María|last9=Soria Morán|first10=Saúl|last10=Chávez|first11=Bertha|last11=Chávez Moreno|first12=Gualberto|last12=Chávez Moreno|first13=Oscar|last13=Roca|first14=Erlin|last14=Siripi|date=10 October 2017|journal=Journal of Ethnobiology and Ethnomedicine|volume=13|issue=1|pages=57|doi=10.1186/s13002-017-0179-2|pmid=29017576|pmc=5634836 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Who should conduct ethnobotanical studies? Effects of different interviewers in the case of the Chácobo Ethnobotany project, Beni, Bolivia|first1=Narel Y.|last1=Paniagua-Zambrana|first2=Rainer W.|last2=Bussmann|first3=Robbie E.|last3=Hart|first4=Araceli L.|last4=Moya-Huanca|first5=Gere|last5=Ortiz-Soria|first6=Milton|last6=Ortiz-Vaca|first7=David|last7=Ortiz-Álvarez|first8=Jorge|last8=Soria-Morán|first9=María|last9=Soria-Morán|first10=Saúl|last10=Chávez|first11=Bertha|last11=Chávez-Moreno|first12=Gualberto|last12=Chávez-Moreno|first13=Oscar|last13=Roca|first14=Erlin|last14=Siripi|date=26 January 2018|journal=Journal of Ethnobiology and Ethnomedicine|volume=14|issue=1|pages=9|doi=10.1186/s13002-018-0210-2|pmid=29373988|pmc=5787299 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Bussmann is editor-in-chief of ''Ethnobotany Research and Applications'', deputy editor of the ''[[Journal of Ethnobiology and Ethnomedicine]]'', associate editor of ''Ethnobiology and Conservation'', academic editor of ''[[PLOS One]]'', editor of ethnobotany topics for the ''[[Nordic Journal of Botany]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/login/|title=Log In or Sign Up to View|website=www.facebook.com}}</ref> and member of the editorial boards of ''Antibiotics'', ''Life'', ''Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge'', ''Pleione'' and ''[[Nelumbo]]''.

He has been involved in the development of professional societies in the field of ethnobotany and ethnobiology as president and member of the council of the [[Society for Economic Botany]] (2008–2020),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://econbot.org/home/governance/society-officers.html|title=The Society for Economic Botany|website=econbot.org}}, and board member of the</ref> International Society for Ethnopharmacology (2010–2014), Society of Ethnobiology (2008–2011), [[Botanical Society of America]] (2008–2011), International Society of Ethnobiology (2008–2010), and holds memberships in the [[Aetat|Association for the Taxonomic Study of the Flora of Africa]], Bayerische Botanische Gesellschaft, East Africa Natural History Society, International Society of Ethnobiology, International Society for Ethnopharmacology, [[Society for Economic Botany]], and Society of Ethnobiology.
In addition to his academic work, Bussmann has co-founded several international non-governmental organizations in the areas of Biodiversity Conservation and Traditional Knowledge, including Nature and Culture International, Saving Knowledge and Etnomont. He featured in the German television documentary ''Secret world of herbs.''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Filmquadrat Kräuterwelten in Südamerika - Dokumentation - filmquadrat.dok|url=https://www.filmquadrat.de/filme/533/The-Secret-World-of-Herbs--In-South-America/|website=www.filmquadrat.de}}</ref>

Bussmann receives International Ethnopharmacologist of the Year Award|website=ILIA STATE UNIVERSITY|accessdate=18 April 2023}}</ref>
* Ilia Chavchavadze Medal for Scientific Excellence 2021. Instituted in 2017 to commemorate the 200 birthday of Ilia Chavchavadze, the Ilia Medal is awarded annually to scientists for excellence in science and scholarship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iliauni.edu.ge/en/siaxleebi-8/axali-ambebi-36/ilia-medal-awarded-to-isu-professors-listed-among-the-worlds-top-scientists.page|title=Ilia Medal awarded to ISU Professors listed among the world's top scientists|website=ILIA STATE UNIVERSITY}}</ref>
* James Duke Award of the American Botanical Council 2012 por la publicación "Medicinal Plants and the Legacy of Richard E. Schultes".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.herbalgram.org/news/press-releases/2013/gladstar_to_receive_blumenthal_award/|title=ABC Announces Recipients of James A. Duke Excellence in Botanical Literature Award – American Botanical Council|date=7 August 2021|website=www.herbalgram.org}}</ref>
* Two botanical species were named after Bussmann. ''Poa bussmannii'' H. Scholz described on 2011,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77109251-1|title=Poa bussmannii H.Scholz &#124; Plants of the World Online &#124; Kew Science|website=Plants of the World Online}}</ref> which has Turkey as its native range. ''Gentianella bussmannii'' J.S. Pringle, described in 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77175752-1|title=Gentianella bussmannii J.S.Pringle &#124; Plants of the World Online &#124; Kew Science|website=Plants of the World Online}}</ref> is a native species of the Peruvian Andes.

== Publications ==
Bussmann is the author of 450 peer-reviewed articles, more than 1,300 book chapters, and is the author / editor of 38 books.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=es&user=jvsdlkIAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&gmla=AJsN-F4sIv-FDryg2zq-qC-1S9b5_NnVCPcNx8qqSlV7qaXnq1C5mmUc-3Uu4h2Kv2nMxyyV3zzqL7qTQ517eCrUZb4RvY_RCcv2THjaG9jee_UjMAmnIYNkDxIiPrJxVOC16rvTrpKGC3am9Dep6lW9l9G8DKxTHU_V_VKBqvM0JfrMA9nbGdMPKbhkN5PJJXrnvQosATm9sWe8JVUlcrAiyXcsyWUKpw&sciund=7801836191896711947|title = Rainer W. Bussmann}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3524-5273|title = ORCID}}</ref> According to Elsevier, he is one of the most cited ethnobotanists and recognized among the most influential scientists worldwide.<ref name="n232">{{citation | last1=Ioannidis | first1=John P.A. | author2=Stanford University | title=August 2025 data-update for "Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators" | chapter=Bibliometrics | date=19 September 2025 | volume=8 | doi=10.17632/BTCHXKTZYW.8 | url=https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btchxktzyw/8 | access-date=22 October 2025 | page= | publisher=Elsevier Data Repository }}</ref> He currently serves as editor-in-chief of the "Ethnobotany of Mountain Regions" book series published by Springer Nature.<ref name="Ethnobotany of Mountain Regions">{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/series/15885|title=Ethnobotany of Mountain Regions|via=www.springer.com}}</ref>
